actor.why: One row per actor keyed by actor_id with first and last name; film_actor points at it; last_update is audit.

address.why: One row per postal address keyed by address_id, pointing at city; customer, staff and store point at it.

category.why: 16 film category names keyed by category_id, pointed at only by film_category.

city.why: 600 cities keyed by city_id, pointing at country; address points at it. A place in a geographic hierarchy rather than a code label.

country.why: 109 country names keyed by country_id, pointed at only by city.

customer.why: One row per customer keyed by customer_id, pointing at store and address; rental and payment point at it; create_date and last_update are audit-like.

film.why: One row per film keyed by film_id, pointing at language; inventory, film_actor and film_category point at it.

film_actor.why: Pure link of actor_id and film_id, keyed by the pair, with only an audit last_update.

film_category.why: Pure link of film_id and category_id, keyed by the pair, with only an audit last_update.

film_text.why: One row per film keyed by film_id with title and description, a one-to-one copy of film's text kept for full-text search.

inventory.why: One row per physical copy keyed by inventory_id, pointing at film and store; rental points at it.

language.why: Six language names keyed by language_id, pointed at only by film (through language_id and original_language_id).

payment.why: One row per payment, stamped with payment_date, pointing at customer, staff and rental.

rental.why: One row per rental, stamped with rental_date, pointing at inventory, customer and staff; payment points at it.

staff.why: Two staff members keyed by staff_id with names, email and address; rental, payment and store point at it.

store.why: Two stores keyed by store_id with a manager and an address; customer, staff and inventory point at it.
